observed_mechanics: 0x00643a40: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0xc] reads the tree root, which is the anchor's parent word; the anchor itself is at ECX+4 (0x00643a48 LEA ESI,[ECX + 0x4]) and is the end() sentinel used at 0x00643a6a.

0x00643a58: CMP dword ptr [EAX + 0x10],EBP reads the node key at +0x10; 0x00643a5b JC takes the child at +0x0 when node.key < target and 0x00643a5f MOV EAX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x4] takes the child at +0x4 otherwise, with 0x00643a5d MOV EDX,EAX remembering the candidate. This is a lower_bound walk over a red-black tree whose node links are at +0 (right) and +4 (left).

0x00643a70/0x00643a73: the hit test is target >= candidate.key; combined with the walk invariant (a candidate is only kept when its key is >= the target) this is an exact-equality test, so the fast path can only fire on a real match.
0x00643ab3: LEA EAX,[EDX + 0x14] returns the address of the matched node's 4-byte mapped slot.
0x00643a77/0x00643a94: the miss path materialises {*key, 0} in the 8-byte frame slot, i.e. a default-constructed mapped value of zero.
0x00643a7b/0x00643a80/0x00643aa1: the caller's own argument word is zeroed, pushed, and re-read after the call, so it doubles as the out-parameter for the created node.
0x00643a9c: CALL 0x006432d0 passes ECX = the container plus four stack words (&argument word, candidate, &value pair, 0); 0x006432d0 retires them with RET 0x10.

0x00579b50 (reached from 0x006432d0): *(int *)(param_1 + 0x14)++ proves the container field at +0x14 is the node counter, and *param_2 = iVar1 proves the insert path publishes the created node through the address of the caller's argument word, which is what 0x00643aa1 reads back.

0x00579b50 also carries the assert string "EASTL\include\EASTL/allocator.h", which identifies the container as EASTL, and asserts an allocation size of 0x18, matching rbtree_node_base (13 bytes padded to 16) plus an 8-byte pair.

0x00644510 and 0x00644530: the same function reached through two-instruction wrappers that store a 4-byte value through the returned pointer, with the container at receiver+0x10 and receiver+0x2c respectively - the observed map[key] = value shape, and the 0x1c stride between the two containers.
0x00fede40: MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x8],EAX / CALL 0x00643a40 / MOV dword ptr [EAX],0x1 / RET 0x4 - the same find-or-insert used as map[key] = 1 on the container at receiver+0x5c.
0x00643db0: after the call the result is dereferenced (0x00643df7 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EAX]) and, when non-null, called (0x00643dfd CALL EAX), so at least one mapped value is a function pointer.

0x00584300 (Editors::cEditor::Initialize) calls the function six times with the keys 0x3d97a8e4, 0x2b978c46, 0x2399be55, 0x24682294, 0x476a98c7 and 0x438f6347 on the container at cEditor+0x1b0 and stores the values 0x3615a30b, 0x465c50ba, 0xd817cd63, 0x99f87089, 0x96b24187 and 0x1c7eca95 into the returned slots; the same six keys are the reserved keys that 0x00643db0 rejects (0x00643e0f pushes 0x13ff778 and 0x78 and calls 0x00f473a0).

sdk_correspondence.observation: The container is EASTL. 0x00579b50 embeds the assert path "EASTL\include\EASTL/allocator.h" and an allocation size of 0x18; the node field order (right, left, parent, colour, value at +0x10) and the container shape (anchor at +0x04, root in the anchor's parent word at +0x0c, counter at +0x14) match EASTL-3.02.01/include/EASTL/internal/red_black_tree.h (rbtree_node_base, rbtree::mAnchor then mnSize then mAllocator), and ~/apps/Spore-ModAPI ships exactly that EASTL-3.02.01 tree.
sdk_correspondence.not_asserted: No Spore ModAPI class name is claimed for the receiver. The container is a bare map sub-object and its owning class differs per callsite (+0x10, +0x2c, +0x5c, +0x1b0), so no single owner can be named.

semantic_contract: Find-or-insert accessor of an EASTL ordered map whose key and mapped value are both 4 bytes. Given a pointer to the key it walks the red-black tree for the exact match, keeping the last node whose key is >= the target. If that node's key equals the target, the address of its mapped slot is returned unchanged. Otherwise the function builds {key, 0} in its own frame, calls the insert helper 0x006432d0 with the walk's candidate as the insertion hint, and returns the address of the mapped slot of the node the helper created. The tree root, the end() sentinel, the node links, the key offset, the mapped offset and the node counter are all fixed by the instructions above; the node size is 0x18.
classification_rationale: Body, ABI, frame, every field offset, every constant, the full control flow and the single callee's contract are read directly from the disassembly and corroborated by three wrapper call sites and the EASTL assert string, so the mechanics are not in doubt. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because two material elements stay bounded: the owning class of the container is unknown (four different sub-offsets are used by different callers) and the domain meaning of the 4-byte keys and mapped values is not established - the observed usages are registration of 32-bit hashes, a boolean 1 and a function pointer, which is consistent with a class/type registry but does not prove it.
semantic_findings: The function is a find-or-insert (operator[]-shaped) accessor over an EASTL map, not a plain lookup: a miss mutates the tree and bumps the counter at +0x14.
The return value is a pointer to the mapped slot, not the mapped value: every inspected caller writes through it.
The miss path passes the walk's candidate as an insertion hint, so a miss on a key that sorts between two existing nodes inserts adjacent to the candidate rather than re-walking from the root.
The incoming argument word is reused as the out-parameter for the created node; this is proved by 0x00579b50's *param_2 = iVar1 and by the address of that word being handed down the call chain.
The container is 0x1c bytes and holds exactly one map; callers place it at different offsets inside different owners.

Six 32-bit key values are treated as reserved by a sibling reader (0x00643db0) while cEditor::Initialize writes six distinct hashes under exactly those keys, so the reserved keys are registered values rather than sentinels.
unresolved_questions: Which class owns each container? Four different sub-offsets (+0x10, +0x2c, +0x5c, +0x1b0) are used by different callers and no vtable was located for any of the owners.
What do the 4-byte keys and mapped values denote? The observed values look like class-name hashes but nothing in the binary names the registry.
Why does 0x00643db0 treat the six keys that cEditor::Initialize registers as assert-failures? The relationship between the registration and the rejection is not established.

In the 0x006432d0 path that reaches 0x00579bd0 instead of 0x00579b50, the published node appears to be written into the value pair rather than the argument word, which would leave the 0x00643aa1 reload reading the zeroed word. Static stack arithmetic does not settle which write the compiler contracted for; the primary path is settled, this one is not.
The container word at +0x00 and the node word at +0x0c are unobserved here, so their identity (comparator, allocator, colour) is inferred from the EASTL header rather than read.

Whether the 0xffffff00 masking the decompiler shows on the argument pointer (an artefact of the byte-sized zeroing at 0x00643a7b) has any effect on keys whose address is not 256-byte aligned. Every inspected callsite passes a stack address, which is not 256-byte aligned in general, so the port keeps the observed behaviour of zeroing the low byte of the argument word.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this address; every claim is static.

A runtime differential test would be needed to confirm that the reserved-key rejection in 0x00643db0 and the registration in cEditor::Initialize are reproduced, and that no runtime patch retargets the container.
The identity of the owning class can only be settled with a receiver trace or a located vtable.

result_summary: Find-or-insert accessor of a 4-byte-keyed EASTL ordered map. It walks the red-black tree from the root stored at container+0x0c, returns the address of the matching node's 4-byte mapped slot, and on a miss inserts {key,0} through 0x006432d0 and returns the new node's mapped slot. Wrappers at 0x00644510, 0x00644530 and 0x00fede40 use it as map[key] = value.
